Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 65, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Talaq (Divorce), because it explains the rulings of divorce and its manner, and what follows from it of rulings concerning the 'iddah (waiting period), maintenance (nafaqah), and residence (sukna).

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Explaining the rulings of divorce, what follows it of the 'iddah ('iddah) and its types, and what relates to that of matters of breastfeeding, maintenance, and residence.

• Commanding that one stop at the limits of Allah and not disobey His commands, calling to the fear of Allah (taqwa), warning against transgressing His limits, and presenting the example of the rebellious nations that defied the command of Allah and so tasted the evil consequence and the punishment.

[The Tafsir]

﴿O Prophet, when you (and the believers with you) intend to divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period,﴾ that is, in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse, or while they are visibly pregnant. ﴿And count the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord.﴾ Keep count of the 'iddah so that you may know the time for taking them back, if you wish to take them back. ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immoral act,﴾ such as adultery. The divorced women are not to be removed from the homes in which they reside until their waiting period ends, and it is three menstrual cycles for a woman who is not a minor, not past menopause, and not pregnant. It is not permissible for them to leave those homes on their own. ﴿These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself.﴾ He has brought himself to ruin. ﴿You do not know, O divorcer, that perhaps Allah will bring about after that divorce some matter you do not expect, so that you may take her back.﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 65, verse 2–3:

When the divorced women have nearly reached the end of their waiting period (ʿidda), then either take them back with good treatment and by providing for them, or part from them while giving them their due rights, without harming them. And call upon two just men from among you to bear witness to the taking back or the parting, and, O witnesses, give your testimony sincerely for the sake of Allah alone, not for anything else. This is what Allah has commanded you, and it is with this that admonition is given to those who believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, acting on what He has commanded him and avoiding what He has forbidden him, Allah will make for him a way out of every hardship, and will facilitate for him the means of provision from where he does not expect and does not reckon. And whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him in every matter that concerns him in all his affairs. Indeed, Allah accomplishes His command; nothing escapes Him, and nothing sought can overpower Him. Allah has set for everything a term at which it ends, and a measure which it does not exceed.

And the divorced women who have stopped menstruating due to their old age—if you are in doubt and do not know the ruling concerning them—their waiting period (ʿiddah) is three months; and likewise the young girls who have not yet menstruated, their waiting period is three months as well. As for women who are pregnant, their waiting period is that they give birth to their burden. And whoever fears Allah, by carrying out His commands, He will make for him ease in his affair in this world and the Hereafter.

That which has been mentioned of the rulings on divorce and the waiting period is the command of God, which He has sent down to you, O people, so that you may act upon it. And whoever fears God and is mindful of Him by avoiding His prohibitions and performing His obligations, He will remove his sins from him, multiply his reward in the Hereafter, and admit him into Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 65, verse 6:

﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means, from wherever you have wealth, and do not harass them so as to constrict them.﴾ That is, house the divorced women among your wives during their waiting period ('iddah), in a dwelling like your own, according to your capacity and ability, and do not cause them harm so as to squeeze them in their housing. And if your divorced wives are pregnant, then spend on them during their waiting period until they deliver their burden. If they nurse your children for you for a wage, then give them their wages. Let some of you enjoin on others what is known to be kindly and generous of spirit. And if you do not agree on the nursing by the mother, then another wet-nurse other than the divorced mother shall be hired for the father.

Let the husband spend from what Allah has granted him in abundance on his divorced wife and on his child, if the husband is wealthy in provision. And whoever has his provision restricted, being poor, let him spend from what Allah has given him of provision. Allah does not burden the poor man with what He burdens the rich man. Allah will bring ease after hardship and difficulty, and abundance and wealth.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 65, verses 8–9:

And many a city rebelled against the command of its Lord and of His messengers, and they persisted in their transgression and disbelief. So We called them to a severe reckoning for their deeds in this world, and We punished them with a dreadful, terrible punishment. Thus they tasted the evil consequence of their arrogance and disbelief, and the outcome of their disbelief was destruction and a loss after which there is no loss.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 65, verses 10–11:

Allah has prepared for these people who transgressed and opposed His command and the command of His messengers a severe punishment. So fear Allah and beware of His wrath, O people of sound intellect who believed in Allah and His messengers and acted according to His law. ﴿Allah has certainly sent down to you, O believers, a reminder﴾ that reminds you of it and alerts you to your share of faith in Allah and of acting in obedience to Him. This reminder is the Messenger, who recites to you the clear verses of Allah, clarifying for you the truth from falsehood, ﴿that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into light﴾. Those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, and acted upon what Allah commanded them and obeyed Him, will be brought out from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever.﴾ Beneath their palaces and trees flow the rivers, and they will abide in them forever. Allah has certainly made good provision for the righteous believer in Paradise.

Allah alone is the One who created seven heavens, and created seven earths like them. He sends down His command, which He revealed to His messengers, and the affairs by which He manages the conditions of His creation between the heavens and the earth, so that you may know, O people, that Allah has power over everything, nothing being beyond His ability, and that Allah has encompassed everything in knowledge, so nothing escapes His knowledge and power.
